title: What does a WCAG conformance level require?
answer: A level asks for its own criteria and those of the levels below it, in the WCAG version you name

checks.question: A site meets all 24 criteria labelled AA in WCAG 2.2 but fails 1.1.1 Non-text Content, a level A criterion. Does it conform at level AA?
checks.answer: No. Level AA’s list includes every level A criterion, so failing one level A criterion fails level AA too, however many AA criteria pass.

checks.question: A contract asks for WCAG 2.1 level AA. A team checked its pages against the WCAG 2.2 level AA list and met all 55. What is still unchecked, and what did they check that 2.1 does not ask for?
checks.answer: 4.1.1 Parsing is still unchecked: it is on the 2.1 AA list of 50 but 2.2 removed it. The six criteria 2.2 added at A or AA are extra work for a 2.1 contract.

checks.question: Keyboard focus on a new site is invisible. Does that fail 2.4.7 Focus Visible under a WCAG 2.0 level A policy, a WCAG 2.2 level A policy, or a WCAG 2.2 level AA policy?
checks.answer: Only under the 2.2 level AA policy. 2.4.7 is a level AA criterion in 2.0, 2.1 and the final 2.2 text, so neither level A list includes it, although drafts of 2.2 had moved it to level A.

steps.title: Level AAA asks for 86 criteria in WCAG 2.2
steps.line: Each row includes the rows above it.
steps.caption: Does aiming for AA mean checking the criteria labelled AA? WCAG’s conformance requirements say a level AA page satisfies all the level A and level AA criteria, or offers an alternate version that does, so level AA’s list in WCAG 2.2 is 31 at level A plus 24 at AA. At level AAA, the selected level, the list holds 86 criteria, 8 of them under guideline 2.5. A count names the set to evaluate; it is not a conformance result.
